newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil edge up on crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil edge up on crude.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps edged up at midday on Thursday in quiet trading as sentiment improved following firmer overnight crude values and expectations that the market might have bottommed, traders said.
"The gas oil is picking up because some people think the market might have been overdone," one trader said.
July swaps were quoted at $22.45/$22.55 per barrel, August at $22.85/$23.00, both up about 15 cents from Wednesday, brokers said.
Traders said the firmer prices were also due to expectations that the market might have hit bottom after recent aggressive offers by a European major.
The major on Wednesday sold a July 10-14 lifting cargo at Singapore spot quotes minus 65 cents free-on-board basis with another cargo sold by a Malaysian trader at $22.00 for July 21-25 lifting.
Traders said demand is likely to pick up over the next few weeks on fresh Chinese demand after the handover as the authorities there are currently coming down hard on oil smugglers.
Enduser demand is high with stocks in China said low due to the relatively low level of smuggling imports over the past month, they said.
Supply is expected to tighten because the arbitrage from the West is closed with a lot of the July Middle East barrels committed to India which had bought 855,000 tonnes for July delivery.

The swaps regrade remained wide on fresh buying from a trader looking to hedge his sale to Taiwan for 32,000 tonnes of jet fuel for Aug 1-10 delivery at just under $197.00 per tonne on a cost-and-freight basis, traders said.
July swaps regrade was bid at $2.00 per barrel while August was bid at $1.75, both unchanged from Wednesday.
Fuel oil were steady with $99.75/$100.50 per tonne.
